title: Viz HCM flags hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a 61-year-old man with dizziness at Cleveland Clinic, and mavacamten eases his symptoms
summary: Viz HCM gave a 61-year-old man's electrocardiogram a probability above 0.95 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; imaging confirmed the disease, and mavacamten eased his symptoms by week 8.
account: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Viz HCM De Novo classification on 3 August 2023. Its reviewers found that the probable benefits outweigh the probable risks despite a low positive predictive value. A 61-year-old man, unaware of any cardiomyopathy, had lightheadedness, dizziness, fatigue and functional limitation on moderate exertion. He had a baseline electrocardiogram (ECG) at an executive physical at Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio (no date given). Clinicians read it as normal sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block. Under an organization-wide initiative the ECG was uploaded to a cloud platform running the Viz HCM convolutional neural network. The algorithm gave a probability above 0.95 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and he was referred to the Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center. Echocardiography showed 2 cm basal septal hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion and a post-exercise outflow gradient of 72 mm Hg. He started mavacamten 5 mg daily after shared decision-making, and by week 8 the resting gradient was 9 mm Hg. He had less dizziness and dyspnea and no hospitalizations. Cleveland Clinic's hypertrophic cardiomyopathy team reported on 17 March 2025 that the hospital analyzed every ECG for the disease from 19 February 2024 to 1 November 2024. Of the 1,265 patients that the algorithm flagged, 63 received a new diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
purpose: Viz HCM is a cloud-based AI-ECG algorithm built to flag probable hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from 12-lead ECGs. This diagnosis is its intended function.
segment: AI-ECG screening in a health system

ratings.reason: An undiagnosed obstructive cardiomyopathy causing dizziness and exertional limitation was identified and treated with a disease-specific drug. Gradient reduction and symptom improvement at 8 weeks are documented. Long-term benefit is not yet shown.

ai_role.statement: The AI-ECG probability (>0.95) was the trigger for referral and echocardiography in a patient not previously suspected of HCM. Imaging confirmed the diagnosis and clinicians chose the treatment. Disclosed relationships: Dr Desai is a consultant for and has research agreements with Viz-ai (among other companies). Mrs Rutkowski is a consultant for Viz-ai. Mrs Ospina has none. All three authors are listed under the Cleveland Clinic Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center, with no Viz.ai affiliation.
